observations: The lower-right motif is located: a narrow upright stem rises from a spreading basal root system and curves into a broad green blade with a serrated underside and a curled right extremity. Several ordinary short writing lines occupy the white space to the right of the upright stem and below/left of the green blade. They are not written on the green mass. This is not a clearly closed caption cell. Whether the unpainted concavity was intended as an inside surface of a folded leaf is not visually resolved; the white region is also compatible with exterior background between stem and blade. The line lengths follow available white space. I see no writing stroke demonstrably functioning as a vein, stem or blade outline.
limitations: Source-selected exploratory observation after reading the historical PVO enclosure claim; not independent discovery of this motif.
No lexical reading, source-locus mapping, anatomy/name translation or pigment chronology attempted.
Absence of clear shared strokes in this one selected interface does not refute every iconic code.
PVO inside-body ownership cannot be affirmed from my observation; enclosure of a concavity is not the same as writing on a drawn plant surface.
